hints.title: Cascading Elimination Obstacle
hints.text: Asteroids moving right and left can trigger chained destructions across prior survivors. How can an ordered history of right-moving survivors resolve incoming left-moving bodies efficiently?

hints.title: Opposing Direction Invariant
hints.text: A collision occurs if and only if the top of the history moves right (>0) and the incoming asteroid moves left (<0). All other direction combinations never collide.

hints.title: Collision Resolution Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through asteroids. While the current asteroid moves left and the top of the history moves right, compare their absolute sizes: if top is smaller, pop top and continue; if equal, pop top and destroy current; if top is larger, destroy current. If current survives, append it.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Each asteroid is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly scanning the array to find and remove adjacent colliding pairs takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using an auxiliary list to store surviving asteroids bounds each element to amortized O(1) operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly identifying that left-moving asteroids preceding right-moving ones never collide.
